sections.h2: How a Mercer Island sale works
sections.html:
An agent, a do-it-yourself sale and a cash purchase by someone who accepts the house untouched are the three paths here. At the end of each, you sign a deed, file an excise tax affidavit and record with King County.

The island sits in the southern half of Lake Washington, Seattle to the west and Bellevue to the east, and the city limits match the island. As of July 1, 2025, an estimated 25,422 people live on 6.38 square miles of land. Owners occupy 67.0 percent of homes, and the median owner-occupied value reaches $2,000,000 or more. Median household income is $219,069 and median gross rent is $2,502.

No showings, no repair list and no waiting on a buyer's loan: that is the pull of cash. A tidy, permitted, photo-ready house can still earn more on the open market. About 22.2 percent of residents are 65 or older, and many owners stay put for years, so inherited and downsizing sales are common. If you have owned a long time, pull the permit history first, because it shows which additions and remodels the city has on file.

Washington taxes a sale with a graduated real estate excise tax, and the seller usually pays. State rates start at 1.10 percent and top out at 3 percent. For closings from January 1, 2027 the bands break at $551,000, $1,551,000 and $3,051,000. Earlier closings break at $525,000 and $1,525,000 for the first two. At island prices a large share of a sale falls in the upper bands.

Your title officer can quote the exact total, local rate included, for your closing date. Payment is owed on the sale date, which the Department of Revenue counts as the day the deed is notarized, and tax left unpaid can turn into a lien on the property.

sections.h2: Slopes, seismic areas and hazard maps
sections.html:
The city maps four hazard areas on its GIS portal: seismic, steep slope, erosion and potential slide. If your lot falls in one, work on ground or vegetation usually needs a permit, and buyers will ask about it.

The island is a glacial plateau cut by ravines, and the Seattle Fault crosses its northern part. On lots flagged for erosion, potential slide or steep slope, clearing, grading, filling and foundation work are barred between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver backed by a geotechnical evaluation. A geotechnical report is also required when a structure goes into a critical area.

Check the map before planning any pre-sale repair. A retaining wall or deck fix that is exempt on flat ground can need review on a slope.

The city's Code Compliance planner handles work done without required permits, and a buyer's lender or inspector may ask about past remodels. An exemption from a building permit does not exempt a project from building or land use codes. Under MICC 17.14.010, a permit covers building, enlarging, altering, repairing, moving or demolishing a structure, plus electrical, gas, mechanical and plumbing systems. The city lists 22 exceptions, among them:

ProjectExempt from a building permit when
Shed or playhouseOne story, detached, up to 200 square feet
FenceUp to 6 feet high
Retaining wallUp to 4 feet from the bottom of the footing, flat ground, no surcharge
Deck or drivewayNot more than 30 inches above grade and not over a basement
Re-roofingIn kind, with the sheathing not replaced

None of these exceptions applies in flood hazard areas or critical areas unless the work is entirely inside an existing legal building. Construction hours are 7 a.m. to 7 p.m. Monday through Friday and 9 a.m. to 6 p.m. Saturday, with no work on Sundays or holidays.

Three documents matter: the seller disclosure statement, the deed and the excise tax affidavit. Hand the disclosure over five business days after both parties accept, unless the buyer waives it or an exemption applies. Once delivered, the buyer has three business days to rescind. The form in RCW 64.06.020 asks about title, easements, boundary disputes, assessments, zoning violations, water, sewer and structural problems. Answer from what you actually know, and attach an explanation to every yes.

  • King County Assessor: property report with lot size, present use and year built.
  • King County Recorder's Office: recorded plats, surveys and deeds.
  • MyBuildingPermit.com: status of building and land use permits.
  • City Online Map Portal: permit files, sewer as-builts and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
  • Residential certificate of occupancy: on most island houses, the permit card with the signed final inspection serves as the certificate.

The permit center is at 9611 SE 36th Street, and land use staff take calls at 206-275-7605.

The Mercer Island School District runs seven schools on the island, among them Mercer Island High School and Islander Middle School. Interstate 90 crosses the island, with floating bridges toward Seattle and the East Channel Bridge toward Bellevue, and much of the freeway is capped by the Mercer Island Lid. The Sound Transit 2 Line station in the I-90 median opened on March 28, 2026 and has a park-and-ride with 447 stalls. Work them into your listing, or into the description you give a cash buyer.

Cash is worth a look when time, condition or paperwork would slow a listing. Inherited houses, homes with deferred repairs, properties with old permit gaps and sales with tenants in place are the usual cases.

Compare the net, not the headline. On a listing, subtract state and local excise tax, any agent fee you agree to, repair credits, and carrying costs such as utilities and insurance during the weeks the house sits. On a cash deal, get the funds verified, the closing date in writing, and a clear split of excise tax and title costs. Then ask for an offer on your address and weigh it against the list-and-wait numbers.

faqs.q: Who pays the real estate excise tax when a Mercer Island house sells?
faqs.a: The seller, in most cases. Leave it unpaid and the burden can move to the buyer, and a lien can follow. County treasurer receives it as of the sale date, and the local rate sits on top of the graduated state rate.

faqs.q: Can I sell a Mercer Island house with work that was never permitted?
faqs.a: Yes, but expect questions. The city's Code Compliance planner handles such cases, and the usual fix is a courtesy letter or correction notice. One path is a cash buyer who accepts the house as it is. Another is a listing, where the buyer's inspector or lender may request the permit history.

faqs.q: Does the seller disclosure form apply to every Mercer Island sale?
faqs.a: Generally, for improved residential property, unless the buyer waives it or RCW 64.06.010 exempts the transfer. Delivery is due five business days after acceptance, if the parties do not agree otherwise, and the buyer then has three business days to rescind.

faqs.q: Does a steep or low-lying lot change how I sell on Mercer Island?
faqs.a: It can. The city maps seismic, steep slope, erosion and potential slide hazards. Permit exemptions for flat lots do not apply in critical areas, and ground work on erosion, slide or steep slope lots is limited between October 1 and April 1 unless the city grants a waiver.

faqs.q: Where do I find recorded deeds and the sale history for my Mercer Island property?
faqs.a: The King County Recorder's Office holds recorded plats, surveys and deeds, and the King County Assessor has values and sales history. The city's Online Map Portal also shows permit files and geotechnical reports tied to your parcel.
